purpose: Manage child profiles while retaining disabled data, enforcing capacity and clearly warning before irreversible deletion. Screen-specific role: Re-Enable Confirmation (step-up gated).
edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent attempts to edit a child's DOB after the first save → the field is read-only/locked, with an explanation that changes require Support.
2. A parent disables their only active child while another device still has that child's session active → that device's session is invalidated on its very next API call.
3. A parent initiates permanent deletion, passes step-up, sees the warning, but backs out before final confirmation → no deletion occurs; the profile is entirely unaffected.
4. A parent reorders children while one is mid-deletion-confirmation for a different child → these are independent actions, neither blocks the other.
5. A family's plan capacity decreases while more children are active than the new limit allows, before the parent completes the forced-selection step → a defined safe default applies (most-recently-active child remains enabled) rather than an undefined/inconsistent state.
6. A parent deletes a child profile with an unusual per-child entitlement tied to it → deletion proceeds per the standard flow; entitlement cascade is handled by C.24's own logic.
7. Step-up authentication expires mid-form → re-attempting to save triggers a fresh step-up prompt rather than silently failing or silently saving.
8. Two co-guardians edit the same child's profile from different devices nearly simultaneously → last-write-wins at the database layer; each UI reflects a fresh fetch before allowing a save.
9. A parent deletes the only remaining active child → allowed, with a gentle informational note (not a hard block) that the family will have zero active children.
10. A re-enabled child's notification binding is re-established the next time their profile is selected via Who Is Learning (C.19/B.17), not separately orchestrated here.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Attempt to edit DOB | Field locked/read-only with a brief explanation |
| Add Child beyond plan capacity | Inline block with upsell path |
| Duplicate nickname on save | Inline rejection with differentiation guidance |
| Re-enable beyond plan capacity | Inline block with upsell path |
| Step-up auth expires mid-form | Fresh step-up prompt on save attempt |
| Deletion flow abandoned before final confirm | No action taken; profile unaffected |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero children (after deleting all) → list shows only "+ Add Child" with a friendly prompt.

### 1.13 Loading States
- List: skeleton card-list shimmer. Save: button spinner, rest of form remains visible.

### 1.14 Offline States
- List renders read-only from cache; all mutating actions require connectivity, shown clearly.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; step-up handled entirely by C.19.

**Permanent Deletion (irreversible, self-service):** (1) parent navigates to Child Settings → Delete Child; (2) parent confirms identity via step-up authentication; (3) the app displays the warning *"Deleted data cannot be recovered. This action is permanent."*; (4) on confirmation, deletion executes immediately, subject to legal-retention rules — no Support ticket required; (5) an audited deletion record is created automatically (`child_deletion_cases` → `audit_logs`).
Add/Edit Child reuses the same form fields established in A.1 (nickname, DOB picker, avatar grid, language/level selectors, interest chips, daily-goal slider, AI permission toggle).
**DOB is immutable after first save except via Support** — a hard rule distinguishing DOB from every other editable field, given its role driving age-band content eligibility platform-wide.
**Visible child count is gated by subscription tier** — adding a child beyond plan capacity is blocked inline with a clear upsell path to Subscription & Billing (C.24).
**Duplicate nicknames within a family are rejected inline** at save time, with differentiation guidance offered as the resolution path.
**Trial-cancellation downgrade:** the parent selects the one child who remains active; all others are disabled (not deleted), retaining data, until plan capacity returns.
Every mutating action requires **step-up authentication** via C.19's Parent Gate — mutating endpoints are never reachable with only a standard parent session token.
Re-enabling a disabled child is itself **subject to current plan capacity** — blocked with a clear upsell path if at the limit, never a silent failure.
Revoking a device (C.23) force-logs-out that session immediately.

frame2_status: No independently verified equivalent for this screen; global style inspiration must not replace approved copy
purpose: Explain learning trends for a selected child and safely connect to deeper skill, AI-safety, report and usage-control views. Screen-specific role: Per-Child Report (full view).
edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent selects a date range that spans a period before the child's account even existed → the report correctly shows "no activity" only for the portion of the range after account creation, never an error for the impossible pre-existence portion, and clearly communicates the child's actual account-start boundary if relevant to the parent's understanding.
2. A parent shares an achievement via WhatsApp, but the underlying badge is later revoked due to a data-quality correction (cross-ref A.11 Edge Case 3's "badges are sticky once earned" rule) → the already-shared card remains valid/unaffected (it was generated and sent at a point in time, a static artifact, not a live-updating reference); future report views simply reflect current state without retroactively invalidating a prior share.
3. A parent requests a Safety Report "on demand" for a child with zero blocked requests or content flags ever recorded → the report generates successfully showing a clean/reassuring "no safety events recorded" state, never an error or an empty-looking broken section.
4. AI Insight Report access is requested for a child whose family's premium entitlement expires mid-generation (a race between the async report job and a billing-state change) → the report generation job re-checks entitlement at completion time, not just at request time, and the delivered report respects the entitlement state actually in effect when it's served to the parent.
5. A parent drills into a skill mastery grid item for a skill belonging to a domain the child hasn't engaged with at all yet → shows a clear "not started" state for that skill rather than an empty/confusing detail view, consistent with A.9's `Locked`/`Ready` state language.
6. Two co-guardians view the same child's report on different devices simultaneously and one exports a PDF while the other adjusts the date filter → these are independent, read-mostly view actions with no shared-state conflict requiring coordination (distinct from C.21's mutating-action concurrency concerns).
7. A parent's PDF export or WhatsApp share is requested for a report that itself failed content-safety validation (the underlying weekly/AI-insight report row has `content_safety_passed = false`) → the export/share action operates only against the last *passing* report, exactly mirroring C.20's read-API fallback behavior, never exporting/sharing content that was never eligible to be shown in-app in the first place.
8. A child's AI permission is disabled by the parent partway through a reporting period → the AI Interaction History for that period correctly shows activity only up to the point AI was disabled, with no further entries after that point, and the report doesn't imply ongoing AI activity that didn't actually occur.
9. A parent requests an export/share action while offline → blocked with a clear "needs internet" message, since both actions require a fresh, server-validated report payload, never operating on a potentially-stale local cache for an action with external-sharing consequences.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Report generation delayed | Last successfully generated report shown with explicit "as of" framing (consistent with C.20's established pattern) |
| Zero activity in the selected range/report type | Explicit "no activity yet" / "no safety events recorded" state, never a blank/broken chart |
| AI Insight Report entitlement lapses mid-generation | Delivered report respects entitlement state at serve time, not request time (Edge Case 4) |
| Export/share requested against a content-safety-failed report | Operates against the last passing report instead, mirroring C.20's fallback |
| Export/share requested offline | Blocked with a clear "needs internet" message |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero activity in the selected date range → "Once [Child] starts learning, you'll see their progress here" framing, consistent with the platform's general empty-state philosophy.
- Zero AI interactions/safety events ever → a clean, reassuring "no safety events recorded" state, not an alarming or confusing absence.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Per-Child Report: skeleton shimmer per component, independently resolving (consistent with C.20's per-component independence pattern).
- PDF export: a clear "Generating your report..." progress indicator given the few-second generation time.

### 1.14 Offline States
- The in-app report view renders from cache when offline (read-only, consistent with C.20); export/share actions are blocked offline per Edge Case 9.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; WhatsApp sharing uses the standard OS share sheet, which itself may surface its own permission/app-selection UI outside this app's control.

Treat distinct scoped views or seek approval for merge; do not silently present full history in safety-only report.

functional_requirements.requirement: Per-Child Report components: weekly trend chart, habit calendar, skill mastery grid, AI interaction log link, share-report button (source: screen catalog "Components").
Per-Child Report actions: filter by date range, drill into a skill, export PDF, share via WhatsApp (parent-gated) (source: screen catalog "Actions").
Entry points: Parent Dashboard, Child Management; exit points: AI Interaction History, Screen Time & Bedtime Settings (source: screen catalog "Entry/Exit Points").
**Delayed-analytics and no-activity states are shown explicitly rather than as an empty chart** (source: screen catalog "Navigation Rules").
**Reports never include raw AI chat transcripts, only flags** (source: Parent Area screen table — a hard, zero-exception rule governing the AI Interaction History and Safety Report specifically).

Four report types and their cadence (canonical, source §6.7 "Detailed Workflow"): **Weekly child report** (stories completed, Quran progress, duas learned, habit streaks, quiz scores, recommended next step) — weekly; **Monthly family report** (cross-child progress summary, family streaks, content favorites, learning consistency) — monthly; **AI insight report** (strengths, weak areas, suggested next stories/duas/Quran practice, healthy-usage notes) — premium, weekly; **Safety report** (AI usage history, blocked requests, content flags, profile-setting changes) — on demand.

**Dashboard/report content always labels data freshness; uses trend language and recommendations, never judgmental grades** (source §6.7 Validation Rules — restated here as this screen's own content-tone contract, shared with C.20).

**AI-generated parent insights must never diagnose developmental, behavioral, or religious conditions; must never compare siblings; must never present uncertain conclusions as settled facts** (source §6.7 Business Rules — enforced via the same Content Safety Validator write-time gate established in C.20 §3/§5, reused here, not reimplemented).

Parent Monitoring Flow (canonical, source "Parent Monitoring Flow" diagram): Parent Dashboard → Select child → Per-Child Report → parent sees: Weekly AI report, Habit consistency + streak calendar, Strength/weak-area summary, AI interaction history, Screen time + bedtime behavior → if a concerning AI interaction is found, parent adjusts AI controls or disables AI for that child (routes to C.23); if an overuse pattern is found, parent adjusts the screen-time policy (routes to C.23).

**Achievement sharing is parent-gated and PII-free**: the share flow generates a card showing nickname/initial, badge, and no PII — generated only after Parent PIN verification (source: "Reward/Achievement Flow" diagram, cross-ref A.11 FR-12 — restated and applied here as the canonical share-card contract for any report-originated sharing, not just badge-specific sharing).

**Export PDF** produces a parent-facing document containing the same content-governed (no raw transcript, no diagnosis, no sibling comparison) report data as the in-app view — the PDF is not a separate, less-governed data export path.

**Skill mastery grid drill-down** routes into the underlying skill's detail (consistent with A.9's shared Mastery Engine's skill-state model — Locked/Ready/Learning/Practicing/Mastered/Needs Refresh — presented here in parent-friendly, non-raw-score language, consistent with A.9 FR-3's no-raw-score child-facing rule extended here as a parent-facing-but-still-non-raw-score convention, since A.9's broader "no confusing raw model score" principle applies to parent reports too per FR-7's "never judgmental grades" framing).

AI Interaction History entries are derived exclusively from **safety-event and flag records**, never from raw prompt/response logs — this is an architectural data-sourcing constraint, not merely a display-layer redaction (consistent with A.5's zero-retention principle extended here to the broader AI-interaction-logging surface: if the raw data was never retained in re-displayable form in the first place, FR-5's "never raw transcripts" rule is enforced structurally, not just by a UI choice not to render a field that does exist).

Date-range filtering applies consistently across every component on the screen (trend chart, habit calendar, skill grid, AI interaction log) — a single date-range control governs the whole report view, not per-component independent filters.

purpose: Explain learning trends for a selected child and safely connect to deeper skill, AI-safety, report and usage-control views. Screen-specific role: AI Interaction History (full screen).
edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent selects a date range that spans a period before the child's account even existed → the report correctly shows "no activity" only for the portion of the range after account creation, never an error for the impossible pre-existence portion, and clearly communicates the child's actual account-start boundary if relevant to the parent's understanding.
2. A parent shares an achievement via WhatsApp, but the underlying badge is later revoked due to a data-quality correction (cross-ref A.11 Edge Case 3's "badges are sticky once earned" rule) → the already-shared card remains valid/unaffected (it was generated and sent at a point in time, a static artifact, not a live-updating reference); future report views simply reflect current state without retroactively invalidating a prior share.
3. A parent requests a Safety Report "on demand" for a child with zero blocked requests or content flags ever recorded → the report generates successfully showing a clean/reassuring "no safety events recorded" state, never an error or an empty-looking broken section.
4. AI Insight Report access is requested for a child whose family's premium entitlement expires mid-generation (a race between the async report job and a billing-state change) → the report generation job re-checks entitlement at completion time, not just at request time, and the delivered report respects the entitlement state actually in effect when it's served to the parent.
5. A parent drills into a skill mastery grid item for a skill belonging to a domain the child hasn't engaged with at all yet → shows a clear "not started" state for that skill rather than an empty/confusing detail view, consistent with A.9's `Locked`/`Ready` state language.
6. Two co-guardians view the same child's report on different devices simultaneously and one exports a PDF while the other adjusts the date filter → these are independent, read-mostly view actions with no shared-state conflict requiring coordination (distinct from C.21's mutating-action concurrency concerns).
7. A parent's PDF export or WhatsApp share is requested for a report that itself failed content-safety validation (the underlying weekly/AI-insight report row has `content_safety_passed = false`) → the export/share action operates only against the last *passing* report, exactly mirroring C.20's read-API fallback behavior, never exporting/sharing content that was never eligible to be shown in-app in the first place.
8. A child's AI permission is disabled by the parent partway through a reporting period → the AI Interaction History for that period correctly shows activity only up to the point AI was disabled, with no further entries after that point, and the report doesn't imply ongoing AI activity that didn't actually occur.
9. A parent requests an export/share action while offline → blocked with a clear "needs internet" message, since both actions require a fresh, server-validated report payload, never operating on a potentially-stale local cache for an action with external-sharing consequences.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Report generation delayed | Last successfully generated report shown with explicit "as of" framing (consistent with C.20's established pattern) |
| Zero activity in the selected range/report type | Explicit "no activity yet" / "no safety events recorded" state, never a blank/broken chart |
| AI Insight Report entitlement lapses mid-generation | Delivered report respects entitlement state at serve time, not request time (Edge Case 4) |
| Export/share requested against a content-safety-failed report | Operates against the last passing report instead, mirroring C.20's fallback |
| Export/share requested offline | Blocked with a clear "needs internet" message |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero activity in the selected date range → "Once [Child] starts learning, you'll see their progress here" framing, consistent with the platform's general empty-state philosophy.
- Zero AI interactions/safety events ever → a clean, reassuring "no safety events recorded" state, not an alarming or confusing absence.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Per-Child Report: skeleton shimmer per component, independently resolving (consistent with C.20's per-component independence pattern).
- PDF export: a clear "Generating your report..." progress indicator given the few-second generation time.

### 1.14 Offline States
- The in-app report view renders from cache when offline (read-only, consistent with C.20); export/share actions are blocked offline per Edge Case 9.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; WhatsApp sharing uses the standard OS share sheet, which itself may surface its own permission/app-selection UI outside this app's control.

Treat distinct scoped views or seek approval for merge; do not silently present full history in safety-only report.

3. A parent requests a Safety Report "on demand" for a child with zero blocked requests or content flags ever recorded → the report generates successfully showing a clean/reassuring "no safety events recorded" state, never an error or an empty-looking broken section.
4. edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A child is mid-quiz when the daily screen-time limit is reached → the current question is allowed to complete and the score saved, then the rest screen appears — consistent with the platform's general "never lose in-progress reward-eligible progress due to a restriction" principle.
2. A child's bedtime window begins while they are mid-episode of a Story (not specifically a Quran lesson, but a similar "don't cut off mid-content" concern applies) → playback pauses at the nearest natural content boundary (e.g., end of the current scene/segment) rather than literally mid-sentence, generalizing FR-5's Quran-specific example to all content types with a similar respect-for-content-boundaries principle.
3. A parent grants a screen-time override while the child's session is already in the "calm rest screen" blocked state → the override should unblock that same session immediately (the child doesn't need to fully exit and re-enter), consistent with a smooth, non-punitive parent-assist experience.
4. A child is offline when their locally-cached signed policy's grace period expires (e.g., several days of being offline well past the policy's signed validity window) → the app fails closed, applying the most conservative reasonable restriction (e.g., treating it as if the daily limit were already reached) rather than failing open to unlimited use, consistent with FR-4's "never unlimited when disconnected" rule.
5. A parent changes a child's screen-time limit mid-session (e.g., lowering it from another device while the child is actively using the app) → consistent with the platform's general "changes apply at next session" pattern (already established for screen-time/bedtime elsewhere), the active session is not abruptly interrupted by this specific kind of change, though a bedtime-window change taking effect mid-session is a distinct, generally hard-enforced cutoff per FR-2 item 5 regardless of when it was configured (bedtime windows are evaluated against current time continuously, not "locked in" at session start the way a daily-limit value might be).
6. A parent disables AI for a child while that child is mid-recitation-attempt in A.5's pronunciation flow → consistent with A.5's own established edge case (§1.10 Edge Case 2), the in-progress UI gracefully exits to listen-only mode on the next app-state check, never leaving a dangling broken control.
7. Two co-guardians on different devices simultaneously adjust the same child's screen-time limit to different values → standard last-write-wins semantics apply (consistent with the platform's general low-stakes-preference-conflict handling, distinct from the optimistic-concurrency protection applied to higher-stakes actions like child deletion in C.21) — this is a low-risk-enough setting that a simple last-write-wins is acceptable, though the resulting value is always clearly visible to both parents on next view.
8. A Content Age Level override would place a child's eligible band *below* their actual DOB-derived band (a parent choosing more conservative content) → this is fully supported and respected identically to an above-DOB-band override; the system has no asymmetric restriction on which direction a parent can adjust.
9. A device is revoked from Child Locks & Sessions while that device is mid-API-call (e.g., submitting a habit check-in at the exact moment of revocation) → the in-flight request is allowed to complete if it was already authenticated before the revocation took effect (avoiding data loss for an action the child had already legitimately initiated), but any subsequent request from that device fails authentication immediately after.
10. A parent attempts to set a daily screen-time limit of 0 minutes (effectively fully blocking a child) → this is accepted as a valid, if unusual, configuration (a parent's prerogative), resulting in the child immediately seeing the calm rest screen on any session attempt, with no special-casing or warning beyond standard confirmation of the setting being saved.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Device clock manipulated | Server-authoritative counter unaffected; usage evaluated against signed server time |
| Offline beyond signed grace period | Fails closed to the most conservative restriction state (Edge Case 4) |
| Bedtime cutoff mid-content | Stops at the nearest natural content boundary, never mid-word/mid-sentence (FR-5/Edge Case 2) |
| Parent override requested while child is blocked | Unblocks the existing session immediately, no re-entry required (Edge Case 3) |
| AI disabled mid-recitation-attempt | In-progress UI gracefully exits to listen-only on next app-state check (Edge Case 6) |
| Device revoked mid-in-flight-request | Already-authenticated in-flight request completes; subsequent requests fail immediately |

### 1.12 Empty States
- A child with no screen-time policy configured yet → defaults to no daily limit (unrestricted) with a clear "no limit set" indicator on the Controls screen, never an ambiguous blank field.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Controls screens: skeleton form shimmer while current settings load.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Controls screens themselves require connectivity to save changes (server-authoritative); viewing current settings may render from cache with a staleness indicator.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; microphone-related AI Permissions settings here govern *server-side* feature availability, distinct from the OS-level microphone permission itself (both must be true for recording features to appear, per A.5's established pattern).

functional_requirements.requirement: Controls area sections (canonical, source NoorHeroes Blueprint Master Navigation Map): Screen Time, Quiet Hours / Bedtime, AI Permissions, Content Age Level — all reached under Parent Area → Controls.

Restriction Engine Detailed Workflow (canonical, source §6.13, items 1–6): (1) child session starts; app loads the server-signed restriction policy plus the local usage counter; (2) foreground active-learning time increments; background/paused time does not; (3) a warning notification fires at the configured threshold (e.g., 10 minutes remaining); (4) at the limit, the current short activity/question is allowed to finish or save, then new content is blocked and a calm rest screen is shown (e.g., "Mashallah! Great learning today. Time to rest."); (5) bedtime: new sessions are blocked during the bedtime window; existing playback stops at an appropriate boundary (never mid-word in an active Quran lesson); (6) parent override requires Parent Profile verification and creates an audited unlock entry.

**Server is authoritative; local cache is honored only within a signed grace period. Device clock manipulation does not reset usage counters. Multi-device usage is reconciled server-side, not tracked independently per device** (source §6.13 Validation Rules — three hard, zero-exception rules).
**Offline mode enforces the last signed restriction policy rather than allowing unlimited use when disconnected** (source §6.13 Error Handling).

Existing playback stops at an appropriate boundary at bedtime — **never mid-word in an active Quran lesson** (source §6.13 item 5 — a specific, hard content-respect rule distinct from the general "finish the short activity" rule at the screen-time limit, since bedtime cutoffs apply even mid-activity in a way screen-time limits don't, but must still respect natural content boundaries).

AI Permissions per child: disable AI entirely, restrict voice interaction specifically, set language limits, and choose "curated only" mode (source NoorHeroes Blueprint "Parent AI Controls" card: "Parents can disable AI per child, restrict voice interaction, review history, set language limits, and choose 'curated only' mode").

**AI should increase trust, not risk** — every AI Permissions control exists to give parents a strictly more restrictive posture than the platform default, never to unlock capability beyond what the platform's own AI-safety pipeline allows regardless of parent preference (source: AI Rule card — restated as a ceiling principle: parent controls can only narrow AI capability, never expand it past platform-wide safety bounds).

Content Age Level allows a parent to override the system-derived age-band content eligibility for a specific child (e.g., a precocious reader, or conversely a parent wanting more conservative content than the raw DOB-derived band would suggest) — this override interacts with, but never bypasses, the platform's hard age-band-exclusion guarantees elsewhere (cross-ref B.13 Search's hard age-band filter, A.5's domain content eligibility) — it adjusts the *eligible band itself*, which downstream systems then respect exactly as they would the DOB-derived default.

Child Locks & Sessions: configure per-child app lock (PIN/pattern/biometric toggle) and view/revoke the active device list (source: NoorHeroes Blueprint Parent Area screen table, "Child Locks & Sessions — Configure per-child app lock; PIN/pattern/biometric toggle, active device list; Set lock, Revoke device... Revoking a device force-logs-out that session").

**A locked profile opens its own verification screen. Each child can independently use no lock, pattern, PIN, or device biometric. Only salted hashes/OS biometric assertions are stored; raw patterns and PINs are never logged** (source NoorHeroes Blueprint — the configuration-side restatement of C.19's verification-side guarantee; this document owns the *setting* of these values, C.19 owns their *verification*).

Parent override (screen-time extension or bedtime bypass) **requires Parent Profile verification and creates an audited unlock entry** (source §6.13 item 6) — every override is fully traceable, never an invisible or untracked grant.

Every mutating action under Controls requires step-up authentication via C.19's gate — consistent with C.21's identical requirement, this area introduces no separate or weaker authorization mechanism.

Healthy-usage scoring (a derived, parent-facing metric summarizing bedtime behavior, overuse alerts, and session-cap adherence) is computed from the same server-authoritative usage data this engine maintains — it is a read/insight layer on top of Screen Time data, not a separate tracking system (cross-ref C.20/C.22's "healthy-usage and screen-time status" report content, which reads from this engine's data).

purpose: Give verified parents per-child healthy usage, AI, content eligibility and lock/session controls within the platform safety ceiling. Screen-specific role: Quiet Hours / Bedtime Settings (per child).
edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A child is mid-quiz when the daily screen-time limit is reached → the current question is allowed to complete and the score saved, then the rest screen appears — consistent with the platform's general "never lose in-progress reward-eligible progress due to a restriction" principle.
2. A child's bedtime window begins while they are mid-episode of a Story (not specifically a Quran lesson, but a similar "don't cut off mid-content" concern applies) → playback pauses at the nearest natural content boundary (e.g., end of the current scene/segment) rather than literally mid-sentence, generalizing FR-5's Quran-specific example to all content types with a similar respect-for-content-boundaries principle.
3. A parent grants a screen-time override while the child's session is already in the "calm rest screen" blocked state → the override should unblock that same session immediately (the child doesn't need to fully exit and re-enter), consistent with a smooth, non-punitive parent-assist experience.
4. A child is offline when their locally-cached signed policy's grace period expires (e.g., several days of being offline well past the policy's signed validity window) → the app fails closed, applying the most conservative reasonable restriction (e.g., treating it as if the daily limit were already reached) rather than failing open to unlimited use, consistent with FR-4's "never unlimited when disconnected" rule.
5. A parent changes a child's screen-time limit mid-session (e.g., lowering it from another device while the child is actively using the app) → consistent with the platform's general "changes apply at next session" pattern (already established for screen-time/bedtime elsewhere), the active session is not abruptly interrupted by this specific kind of change, though a bedtime-window change taking effect mid-session is a distinct, generally hard-enforced cutoff per FR-2 item 5 regardless of when it was configured (bedtime windows are evaluated against current time continuously, not "locked in" at session start the way a daily-limit value might be).
6. A parent disables AI for a child while that child is mid-recitation-attempt in A.5's pronunciation flow → consistent with A.5's own established edge case (§1.10 Edge Case 2), the in-progress UI gracefully exits to listen-only mode on the next app-state check, never leaving a dangling broken control.
7. Two co-guardians on different devices simultaneously adjust the same child's screen-time limit to different values → standard last-write-wins semantics apply (consistent with the platform's general low-stakes-preference-conflict handling, distinct from the optimistic-concurrency protection applied to higher-stakes actions like child deletion in C.21) — this is a low-risk-enough setting that a simple last-write-wins is acceptable, though the resulting value is always clearly visible to both parents on next view.
8. A Content Age Level override would place a child's eligible band *below* their actual DOB-derived band (a parent choosing more conservative content) → this is fully supported and respected identically to an above-DOB-band override; the system has no asymmetric restriction on which direction a parent can adjust.
9. A device is revoked from Child Locks & Sessions while that device is mid-API-call (e.g., submitting a habit check-in at the exact moment of revocation) → the in-flight request is allowed to complete if it was already authenticated before the revocation took effect (avoiding data loss for an action the child had already legitimately initiated), but any subsequent request from that device fails authentication immediately after.
10. A parent attempts to set a daily screen-time limit of 0 minutes (effectively fully blocking a child) → this is accepted as a valid, if unusual, configuration (a parent's prerogative), resulting in the child immediately seeing the calm rest screen on any session attempt, with no special-casing or warning beyond standard confirmation of the setting being saved.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Device clock manipulated | Server-authoritative counter unaffected; usage evaluated against signed server time |
| Offline beyond signed grace period | Fails closed to the most conservative restriction state (Edge Case 4) |
| Bedtime cutoff mid-content | Stops at the nearest natural content boundary, never mid-word/mid-sentence (FR-5/Edge Case 2) |
| Parent override requested while child is blocked | Unblocks the existing session immediately, no re-entry required (Edge Case 3) |
| AI disabled mid-recitation-attempt | In-progress UI gracefully exits to listen-only on next app-state check (Edge Case 6) |
| Device revoked mid-in-flight-request | Already-authenticated in-flight request completes; subsequent requests fail immediately |

### 1.12 Empty States
- A child with no screen-time policy configured yet → defaults to no daily limit (unrestricted) with a clear "no limit set" indicator on the Controls screen, never an ambiguous blank field.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Controls screens: skeleton form shimmer while current settings load.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Controls screens themselves require connectivity to save changes (server-authoritative); viewing current settings may render from cache with a staleness indicator.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; microphone-related AI Permissions settings here govern *server-side* feature availability, distinct from the OS-level microphone permission itself (both must be true for recording features to appear, per A.5's established pattern).

functional_requirements.requirement: Controls area sections (canonical, source NoorHeroes Blueprint Master Navigation Map): Screen Time, Quiet Hours / Bedtime, AI Permissions, Content Age Level — all reached under Parent Area → Controls.

Restriction Engine Detailed Workflow (canonical, source §6.13, items 1–6): (1) child session starts; app loads the server-signed restriction policy plus the local usage counter; (2) foreground active-learning time increments; background/paused time does not; (3) a warning notification fires at the configured threshold (e.g., 10 minutes remaining); (4) at the limit, the current short activity/question is allowed to finish or save, then new content is blocked and a calm rest screen is shown (e.g., "Mashallah! Great learning today. Time to rest."); (5) bedtime: new sessions are blocked during the bedtime window; existing playback stops at an appropriate boundary (never mid-word in an active Quran lesson); (6) parent override requires Parent Profile verification and creates an audited unlock entry.

**Server is authoritative; local cache is honored only within a signed grace period. Device clock manipulation does not reset usage counters. Multi-device usage is reconciled server-side, not tracked independently per device** (source §6.13 Validation Rules — three hard, zero-exception rules).
**Offline mode enforces the last signed restriction policy rather than allowing unlimited use when disconnected** (source §6.13 Error Handling).

Existing playback stops at an appropriate boundary at bedtime — **never mid-word in an active Quran lesson** (source §6.13 item 5 — a specific, hard content-respect rule distinct from the general "finish the short activity" rule at the screen-time limit, since bedtime cutoffs apply even mid-activity in a way screen-time limits don't, but must still respect natural content boundaries).

AI Permissions per child: disable AI entirely, restrict voice interaction specifically, set language limits, and choose "curated only" mode (source NoorHeroes Blueprint "Parent AI Controls" card: "Parents can disable AI per child, restrict voice interaction, review history, set language limits, and choose 'curated only' mode").

**AI should increase trust, not risk** — every AI Permissions control exists to give parents a strictly more restrictive posture than the platform default, never to unlock capability beyond what the platform's own AI-safety pipeline allows regardless of parent preference (source: AI Rule card — restated as a ceiling principle: parent controls can only narrow AI capability, never expand it past platform-wide safety bounds).

Content Age Level allows a parent to override the system-derived age-band content eligibility for a specific child (e.g., a precocious reader, or conversely a parent wanting more conservative content than the raw DOB-derived band would suggest) — this override interacts with, but never bypasses, the platform's hard age-band-exclusion guarantees elsewhere (cross-ref B.13 Search's hard age-band filter, A.5's domain content eligibility) — it adjusts the *eligible band itself*, which downstream systems then respect exactly as they would the DOB-derived default.

Child Locks & Sessions: configure per-child app lock (PIN/pattern/biometric toggle) and view/revoke the active device list (source: NoorHeroes Blueprint Parent Area screen table, "Child Locks & Sessions — Configure per-child app lock; PIN/pattern/biometric toggle, active device list; Set lock, Revoke device... Revoking a device force-logs-out that session").

**A locked profile opens its own verification screen. Each child can independently use no lock, pattern, PIN, or device biometric. Only salted hashes/OS biometric assertions are stored; raw patterns and PINs are never logged** (source NoorHeroes Blueprint — the configuration-side restatement of C.19's verification-side guarantee; this document owns the *setting* of these values, C.19 owns their *verification*).

Parent override (screen-time extension or bedtime bypass) **requires Parent Profile verification and creates an audited unlock entry** (source §6.13 item 6) — every override is fully traceable, never an invisible or untracked grant.

Every mutating action under Controls requires step-up authentication via C.19's gate — consistent with C.21's identical requirement, this area introduces no separate or weaker authorization mechanism.

Healthy-usage scoring (a derived, parent-facing metric summarizing bedtime behavior, overuse alerts, and session-cap adherence) is computed from the same server-authoritative usage data this engine maintains — it is a read/insight layer on top of Screen Time data, not a separate tracking system (cross-ref C.20/C.22's "healthy-usage and screen-time status" report content, which reads from this engine's data).

purpose: Give verified parents per-child healthy usage, AI, content eligibility and lock/session controls within the platform safety ceiling. Screen-specific role: Content Age Level Settings (per child).
edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A child is mid-quiz when the daily screen-time limit is reached → the current question is allowed to complete and the score saved, then the rest screen appears — consistent with the platform's general "never lose in-progress reward-eligible progress due to a restriction" principle.
2. A child's bedtime window begins while they are mid-episode of a Story (not specifically a Quran lesson, but a similar "don't cut off mid-content" concern applies) → playback pauses at the nearest natural content boundary (e.g., end of the current scene/segment) rather than literally mid-sentence, generalizing FR-5's Quran-specific example to all content types with a similar respect-for-content-boundaries principle.
3. A parent grants a screen-time override while the child's session is already in the "calm rest screen" blocked state → the override should unblock that same session immediately (the child doesn't need to fully exit and re-enter), consistent with a smooth, non-punitive parent-assist experience.
4. A child is offline when their locally-cached signed policy's grace period expires (e.g., several days of being offline well past the policy's signed validity window) → the app fails closed, applying the most conservative reasonable restriction (e.g., treating it as if the daily limit were already reached) rather than failing open to unlimited use, consistent with FR-4's "never unlimited when disconnected" rule.
5. A parent changes a child's screen-time limit mid-session (e.g., lowering it from another device while the child is actively using the app) → consistent with the platform's general "changes apply at next session" pattern (already established for screen-time/bedtime elsewhere), the active session is not abruptly interrupted by this specific kind of change, though a bedtime-window change taking effect mid-session is a distinct, generally hard-enforced cutoff per FR-2 item 5 regardless of when it was configured (bedtime windows are evaluated against current time continuously, not "locked in" at session start the way a daily-limit value might be).
6. A parent disables AI for a child while that child is mid-recitation-attempt in A.5's pronunciation flow → consistent with A.5's own established edge case (§1.10 Edge Case 2), the in-progress UI gracefully exits to listen-only mode on the next app-state check, never leaving a dangling broken control.
7. Two co-guardians on different devices simultaneously adjust the same child's screen-time limit to different values → standard last-write-wins semantics apply (consistent with the platform's general low-stakes-preference-conflict handling, distinct from the optimistic-concurrency protection applied to higher-stakes actions like child deletion in C.21) — this is a low-risk-enough setting that a simple last-write-wins is acceptable, though the resulting value is always clearly visible to both parents on next view.
8. A Content Age Level override would place a child's eligible band *below* their actual DOB-derived band (a parent choosing more conservative content) → this is fully supported and respected identically to an above-DOB-band override; the system has no asymmetric restriction on which direction a parent can adjust.
9. A device is revoked from Child Locks & Sessions while that device is mid-API-call (e.g., submitting a habit check-in at the exact moment of revocation) → the in-flight request is allowed to complete if it was already authenticated before the revocation took effect (avoiding data loss for an action the child had already legitimately initiated), but any subsequent request from that device fails authentication immediately after.
10. A parent attempts to set a daily screen-time limit of 0 minutes (effectively fully blocking a child) → this is accepted as a valid, if unusual, configuration (a parent's prerogative), resulting in the child immediately seeing the calm rest screen on any session attempt, with no special-casing or warning beyond standard confirmation of the setting being saved.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Device clock manipulated | Server-authoritative counter unaffected; usage evaluated against signed server time |
| Offline beyond signed grace period | Fails closed to the most conservative restriction state (Edge Case 4) |
| Bedtime cutoff mid-content | Stops at the nearest natural content boundary, never mid-word/mid-sentence (FR-5/Edge Case 2) |
| Parent override requested while child is blocked | Unblocks the existing session immediately, no re-entry required (Edge Case 3) |
| AI disabled mid-recitation-attempt | In-progress UI gracefully exits to listen-only on next app-state check (Edge Case 6) |
| Device revoked mid-in-flight-request | Already-authenticated in-flight request completes; subsequent requests fail immediately |

### 1.12 Empty States
- A child with no screen-time policy configured yet → defaults to no daily limit (unrestricted) with a clear "no limit set" indicator on the Controls screen, never an ambiguous blank field.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Controls screens: skeleton form shimmer while current settings load.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Controls screens themselves require connectivity to save changes (server-authoritative); viewing current settings may render from cache with a staleness indicator.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; microphone-related AI Permissions settings here govern *server-side* feature availability, distinct from the OS-level microphone permission itself (both must be true for recording features to appear, per A.5's established pattern).

functional_requirements.requirement: Controls area sections (canonical, source NoorHeroes Blueprint Master Navigation Map): Screen Time, Quiet Hours / Bedtime, AI Permissions, Content Age Level — all reached under Parent Area → Controls.

Restriction Engine Detailed Workflow (canonical, source §6.13, items 1–6): (1) child session starts; app loads the server-signed restriction policy plus the local usage counter; (2) foreground active-learning time increments; background/paused time does not; (3) a warning notification fires at the configured threshold (e.g., 10 minutes remaining); (4) at the limit, the current short activity/question is allowed to finish or save, then new content is blocked and a calm rest screen is shown (e.g., "Mashallah! Great learning today. Time to rest."); (5) bedtime: new sessions are blocked during the bedtime window; existing playback stops at an appropriate boundary (never mid-word in an active Quran lesson); (6) parent override requires Parent Profile verification and creates an audited unlock entry.

**Server is authoritative; local cache is honored only within a signed grace period. Device clock manipulation does not reset usage counters. Multi-device usage is reconciled server-side, not tracked independently per device** (source §6.13 Validation Rules — three hard, zero-exception rules).
**Offline mode enforces the last signed restriction policy rather than allowing unlimited use when disconnected** (source §6.13 Error Handling).

Existing playback stops at an appropriate boundary at bedtime — **never mid-word in an active Quran lesson** (source §6.13 item 5 — a specific, hard content-respect rule distinct from the general "finish the short activity" rule at the screen-time limit, since bedtime cutoffs apply even mid-activity in a way screen-time limits don't, but must still respect natural content boundaries).

AI Permissions per child: disable AI entirely, restrict voice interaction specifically, set language limits, and choose "curated only" mode (source NoorHeroes Blueprint "Parent AI Controls" card: "Parents can disable AI per child, restrict voice interaction, review history, set language limits, and choose 'curated only' mode").

**AI should increase trust, not risk** — every AI Permissions control exists to give parents a strictly more restrictive posture than the platform default, never to unlock capability beyond what the platform's own AI-safety pipeline allows regardless of parent preference (source: AI Rule card — restated as a ceiling principle: parent controls can only narrow AI capability, never expand it past platform-wide safety bounds).

Content Age Level allows a parent to override the system-derived age-band content eligibility for a specific child (e.g., a precocious reader, or conversely a parent wanting more conservative content than the raw DOB-derived band would suggest) — this override interacts with, but never bypasses, the platform's hard age-band-exclusion guarantees elsewhere (cross-ref B.13 Search's hard age-band filter, A.5's domain content eligibility) — it adjusts the *eligible band itself*, which downstream systems then respect exactly as they would the DOB-derived default.

Child Locks & Sessions: configure per-child app lock (PIN/pattern/biometric toggle) and view/revoke the active device list (source: NoorHeroes Blueprint Parent Area screen table, "Child Locks & Sessions — Configure per-child app lock; PIN/pattern/biometric toggle, active device list; Set lock, Revoke device... Revoking a device force-logs-out that session").

**A locked profile opens its own verification screen. Each child can independently use no lock, pattern, PIN, or device biometric. Only salted hashes/OS biometric assertions are stored; raw patterns and PINs are never logged** (source NoorHeroes Blueprint — the configuration-side restatement of C.19's verification-side guarantee; this document owns the *setting* of these values, C.19 owns their *verification*).

Parent override (screen-time extension or bedtime bypass) **requires Parent Profile verification and creates an audited unlock entry** (source §6.13 item 6) — every override is fully traceable, never an invisible or untracked grant.

Every mutating action under Controls requires step-up authentication via C.19's gate — consistent with C.21's identical requirement, this area introduces no separate or weaker authorization mechanism.

Healthy-usage scoring (a derived, parent-facing metric summarizing bedtime behavior, overuse alerts, and session-cap adherence) is computed from the same server-authoritative usage data this engine maintains — it is a read/insight layer on top of Screen Time data, not a separate tracking system (cross-ref C.20/C.22's "healthy-usage and screen-time status" report content, which reads from this engine's data).

### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A child is mid-quiz when the daily screen-time limit is reached → the current question is allowed to complete and the score saved, then the rest screen appears — consistent with the platform's general "never lose in-progress reward-eligible progress due to a restriction" principle.
2. A child's bedtime window begins while they are mid-episode of a Story (not specifically a Quran lesson, but a similar "don't cut off mid-content" concern applies) → playback pauses at the nearest natural content boundary (e.g., end of the current scene/segment) rather than literally mid-sentence, generalizing FR-5's Quran-specific example to all content types with a similar respect-for-content-boundaries principle.
3. A parent grants a screen-time override while the child's session is already in the "calm rest screen" blocked state → the override should unblock that same session immediately (the child doesn't need to fully exit and re-enter), consistent with a smooth, non-punitive parent-assist experience.
4. A child is offline when their locally-cached signed policy's grace period expires (e.g., several days of being offline well past the policy's signed validity window) → the app fails closed, applying the most conservative reasonable restriction (e.g., treating it as if the daily limit were already reached) rather than failing open to unlimited use, consistent with FR-4's "never unlimited when disconnected" rule.
5. A parent changes a child's screen-time limit mid-session (e.g., lowering it from another device while the child is actively using the app) → consistent with the platform's general "changes apply at next session" pattern (already established for screen-time/bedtime elsewhere), the active session is not abruptly interrupted by this specific kind of change, though a bedtime-window change taking effect mid-session is a distinct, generally hard-enforced cutoff per FR-2 item 5 regardless of when it was configured (bedtime windows are evaluated against current time continuously, not "locked in" at session start the way a daily-limit value might be).
6. A parent disables AI for a child while that child is mid-recitation-attempt in A.5's pronunciation flow → consistent with A.5's own established edge case (§1.10 Edge Case 2), the in-progress UI gracefully exits to listen-only mode on the next app-state check, never leaving a dangling broken control.
7. Two co-guardians on different devices simultaneously adjust the same child's screen-time limit to different values → standard last-write-wins semantics apply (consistent with the platform's general low-stakes-preference-conflict handling, distinct from the optimistic-concurrency protection applied to higher-stakes actions like child deletion in C.21) — this is a low-risk-enough setting that a simple last-write-wins is acceptable, though the resulting value is always clearly visible to both parents on next view.
8. A Content Age Level override would place a child's eligible band *below* their actual DOB-derived band (a parent choosing more conservative content) → this is fully supported and respected identically to an above-DOB-band override; the system has no asymmetric restriction on which direction a parent can adjust.
9. A device is revoked from Child Locks & Sessions while that device is mid-API-call (e.g., submitting a habit check-in at the exact moment of revocation) → the in-flight request is allowed to complete if it was already authenticated before the revocation took effect (avoiding data loss for an action the child had already legitimately initiated), but any subsequent request from that device fails authentication immediately after.

| Device revoked mid-in-flight-request | Already-authenticated in-flight request completes; subsequent requests fail immediately |

- A child with no screen-time policy configured yet → defaults to no daily limit (unrestricted) with a clear "no limit set" indicator on the Controls screen, never an ambiguous blank field.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Controls screens: skeleton form shimmer while current settings load.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Controls screens themselves require connectivity to save changes (server-authoritative); viewing current settings may render from cache with a staleness indicator.

### 1.15 Permission States

purpose: Present transparent parent-only subscription choices and store-managed billing with server-verified entitlement. Screen-specific role: Subscription & Billing (landing).
edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent starts a 7-day trial, then immediately cancels within the first hour → the trial entitlement remains active (Mobile Family level) for the remainder of the 7 days, since canceling a trial means "don't auto-convert," not "revoke immediately" — consistent with the platform's general "access continues until the period ends" cancellation philosophy applied even to trials.
2. The Play Store webhook for a successful day-7 trial conversion is delayed by several hours → the app continues to honor the last-verified (trial) entitlement through the signed grace window; if the webhook arrives within that window, entitlement updates correctly; if it doesn't arrive before the grace window expires, the reconciliation job queries the store directly to resolve the actual state rather than leaving it ambiguous indefinitely.
3. A parent on Premium Family (8 children, 6 active) downgrades to Mobile Family (4 children) → the system must select which 2 of the 6 active children become disabled; consistent with the trial-cancellation pattern, the parent is prompted to choose, with the deterministic most-recently-active fallback applying if no selection is made within 24 hours, generalized here from "select 1 of many" to "select N of many to keep" as needed for the specific plan-capacity delta.
4. A parent's payment fails, enters the grace period (`PastDue`), and recovers payment on the very last day of the grace window → the account returns to `ActivePaid` and no children are disabled, since the grace period's entire purpose is to avoid disrupting access while payment issues are resolved.
5. A parent restores a purchase on a new device (e.g., after reinstalling the app or switching devices) → the restore-purchase flow re-validates the existing store receipt server-side and re-establishes the correct entitlement state without requiring a new purchase, consistent with standard app-store restore-purchase expectations.
6. A parent attempts to browse premium content while on the Free plan → the content is shown with a lock icon in the relevant parent-approved discovery context (never hidden entirely), and tapping it routes to the Subscription upsell — this premium content is never silently absent from a catalog/browse view.
7. A family's annual plan is approaching its renewal date, and the 7-day reminder notification would fire during the child's configured bedtime window → since this is a parent-facing notification type, not a child-facing one, it is unaffected by the child's own bedtime/quiet-hours configuration (cross-ref C.23's scope being specifically per-child; parent notification timing is governed by the Parent Area's own notification preferences, C.25).
8. A parent's family has children added via different historical plan tiers (e.g., 4 children added while on Premium Family, then downgraded) → the system's enforcement of "how many children may be *active* at once" is always evaluated against the *current* plan, regardless of historical tier at the time each child was originally added — there is no grandfathering of past capacity.
9. Two webhook events for the same underlying billing event arrive (e.g., a retried delivery from the store) → idempotent processing on `provider_event_id` ensures the second delivery is a safe no-op, never double-processing a renewal or cancellation event.
10. A parent attempts to upgrade mid-trial (before day 7) directly to Premium Family rather than waiting for the standard Mobile Family auto-conversion → this is supported as a direct upgrade path; the trial's scheduled day-7 conversion logic is superseded by the explicit upgrade, which takes effect immediately per FR-9's "Upgrade unlocks immediately" rule.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Store webhook delayed | Last verified entitlement honored within a signed grace window; reconciliation job resolves any lingering ambiguity (FR-6) |
| Duplicate webhook delivery | Idempotent on `provider_event_id`, safe no-op on replay (Edge Case 9) |
| Payment failure on renewal | Email/push reminder, grace period (`PastDue`), no child-mode billing messaging at any point |
| Restore-purchase request | Server-side receipt re-validation, entitlement re-established without a new purchase |
| Plan-capacity-reducing downgrade with more active children than the new plan allows | Parent prompted to select which children remain active; deterministic 24-hour fallback if no selection |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero invoice history yet (new subscriber, first billing cycle not yet processed) → friendly "Your first invoice will appear here after your trial converts" framing.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Plan Comparison/Subscription screen: skeleton plan-card shimmer while entitlement/plan data loads.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Subscription screen renders last-cached entitlement/plan state when offline; purchase/upgrade/cancel actions require connectivity and clearly indicate this if attempted offline, given their store-billing-API dependency.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; all purchase actions route through the OS-level Play Store/App Store billing sheet, which has its own standard permission/account context outside this app's control.

functional_requirements.requirement: Plan Comparison (canonical, source §6.9 "Plan Comparison" table): Free Family Starter ($0, 1 active child, basic stories/duas/habits/basic reports, premium content locked, no AI weekly reports, limited offline); Mobile Family ($3/mo or $30/yr, 16.7% savings, 4 children, expanded content, 10 offline downloads, monthly family report, limited AI insights); Premium Family ($5.99/mo or $59/yr, 17.9% savings, 8 children, full story/Quran library, premium animated stories, full offline mode, weekly AI parent reports, advanced dashboard, extra child slots addable later).

Subscription Lifecycle state machine (canonical, source §6.9): `Free → Trial (7-day) → ActivePaid → RenewalPending → ActivePaid (auto-renew success) | PastDue (payment fails) → ActivePaid (recovered) | Free (grace ends); ActivePaid → Canceled → Free (paid period ends); ActivePaid → DowngradeScheduled → Free (next cycle)`.

**Trial Rules** (canonical, source §6.9/§"Yearly Subscription Logic"): (1) parent sees trial length, post-trial price, renewal date, and auto-renew disclosure before confirming; (2) parent confirms through the platform purchase flow (Google Play / App Store) — **never a custom payment form**; (3) trial entitlements (Mobile Family level) activate immediately; (4) on day 7, Mobile Family auto-activates if billing succeeds; **store receipt + signed webhook are the billing source of truth, not client-reported state**.

**Cancellation/Downgrade Rules** (canonical, source §6.9 table): Cancel subscription → paid access remains until the period ends, then reverts to Free limits; Trial cancellation with multiple children → parent selects 1 child to remain active on Free, others become **disabled, not deleted** (progress retained, restored when plan capacity returns), deterministic fallback (most-recently-active child) applies if no selection within 24 hours; Payment failure → parent receives email/push reminder, **child mode never shows billing messaging**; Renewal reminder → annual plans notify 7 days and 24 hours before renewal; Free plan second-child attempt → upgrade prompt shown in **parent mode only**, existing child's data unaffected.

**Entitlement checks apply at:** catalog/home feed, search, content detail, playback start, download manifest, AI features, and child-profile activation/creation (source §6.9 Validation Rules — the canonical, complete list of entitlement checkpoints every consuming feature must implement).

**Store webhook delayed → use last verified entitlement plus a grace window, then reconcile via a dedicated reconciliation job (not silent trust of the webhook alone, since webhook delivery is not guaranteed-once)** (source §6.9 Error Handling).

**The web portal cannot initiate app-store purchases outside provider policy; it may display the active entitlement and direct the parent to the mobile app appropriately. Store-purchase actions route through platform billing APIs only** (source §5 Web business rules / NoorHeroes Blueprint Parent Area screen table — restated as the hard rule governing the web portal's strictly limited billing surface).

**Purchases, AI controls, external links, deletion/export, and profile edits require parent PIN. Child mode never exposes billing or account-management controls** (source NoorHeroes Blueprint — restated as the hard rule this feature's child-mode-invisibility guarantee enforces, consistent with A.2's platform-wide no-billing-content-to-child rule).

**Yearly Billing Flow** (canonical, source §"Billing Flow" card): Trial converts automatically to Mobile Family unless the parent cancels before the trial ends; Auto-renew renews unless the parent cancels before the renewal date; Cancel means access continues until the paid period ends, then returns to Free limits; Upgrade unlocks immediately and keeps all child profiles intact; Trial cancellation/downgrade activates Basic Free with only one child remaining active and additional profiles disabled without data deletion.

**Downgrade never deletes child data; excess profiles become read-only archives, never silently deleted** (source NoorHeroes Blueprint Subscription & Billing screen, "Navigation Rules" — restated; cross-ref C.21's archived-profile read-only display pattern).

Subscription screen components (canonical, source screen catalog): plan card, entitlement list, invoice history, "Manage on Play Store" deep link, cancel flow. Actions: start trial, upgrade, downgrade, cancel renewal, view invoice, retry failed payment. Entry points: Parent Dashboard, paywall upsell, Settings. Exit points: Google Play billing sheet (external), Parent Dashboard.

Billing endpoints (canonical, source API table): `GET /api/v1/billing/plans` (public, cached); `POST /api/v1/billing/subscribe` (Bearer JWT, validates receipt server-side before activation); `POST /api/v1/billing/webhooks/play` (webhook signature, idempotent on `provider_event_id`, feeds reconciliation); `POST /api/v1/billing/reconcile` (internal/Celery, scheduled job reconciling entitlement state vs. provider truth, not user-facing).

Paywall upsell UI is shown **only in the parent area** when a profile limit is reached or premium content is browsed in a parent-approved discovery context — never inside child mode (cross-ref A.2's hard rule, C.20's explicit permission for parent-surface billing messaging).

Premium content items remain **visible with a lock icon** in parent-approved discovery contexts — never hidden entirely. **Locking never deletes progress. Free plan always supports basic Islamic education** (source NoorHeroes Blueprint — restated, cross-ref A.3/A.10's established "locked, not hidden" content pattern).

edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent starts a 7-day trial, then immediately cancels within the first hour → the trial entitlement remains active (Mobile Family level) for the remainder of the 7 days, since canceling a trial means "don't auto-convert," not "revoke immediately" — consistent with the platform's general "access continues until the period ends" cancellation philosophy applied even to trials.
2. The Play Store webhook for a successful day-7 trial conversion is delayed by several hours → the app continues to honor the last-verified (trial) entitlement through the signed grace window; if the webhook arrives within that window, entitlement updates correctly; if it doesn't arrive before the grace window expires, the reconciliation job queries the store directly to resolve the actual state rather than leaving it ambiguous indefinitely.
3. A parent on Premium Family (8 children, 6 active) downgrades to Mobile Family (4 children) → the system must select which 2 of the 6 active children become disabled; consistent with the trial-cancellation pattern, the parent is prompted to choose, with the deterministic most-recently-active fallback applying if no selection is made within 24 hours, generalized here from "select 1 of many" to "select N of many to keep" as needed for the specific plan-capacity delta.
4. A parent's payment fails, enters the grace period (`PastDue`), and recovers payment on the very last day of the grace window → the account returns to `ActivePaid` and no children are disabled, since the grace period's entire purpose is to avoid disrupting access while payment issues are resolved.
5. A parent restores a purchase on a new device (e.g., after reinstalling the app or switching devices) → the restore-purchase flow re-validates the existing store receipt server-side and re-establishes the correct entitlement state without requiring a new purchase, consistent with standard app-store restore-purchase expectations.
6. A parent attempts to browse premium content while on the Free plan → the content is shown with a lock icon in the relevant parent-approved discovery context (never hidden entirely), and tapping it routes to the Subscription upsell — this premium content is never silently absent from a catalog/browse view.
7. A family's annual plan is approaching its renewal date, and the 7-day reminder notification would fire during the child's configured bedtime window → since this is a parent-facing notification type, not a child-facing one, it is unaffected by the child's own bedtime/quiet-hours configuration (cross-ref C.23's scope being specifically per-child; parent notification timing is governed by the Parent Area's own notification preferences, C.25).
8. A parent's family has children added via different historical plan tiers (e.g., 4 children added while on Premium Family, then downgraded) → the system's enforcement of "how many children may be *active* at once" is always evaluated against the *current* plan, regardless of historical tier at the time each child was originally added — there is no grandfathering of past capacity.
9. Two webhook events for the same underlying billing event arrive (e.g., a retried delivery from the store) → idempotent processing on `provider_event_id` ensures the second delivery is a safe no-op, never double-processing a renewal or cancellation event.
10. A parent attempts to upgrade mid-trial (before day 7) directly to Premium Family rather than waiting for the standard Mobile Family auto-conversion → this is supported as a direct upgrade path; the trial's scheduled day-7 conversion logic is superseded by the explicit upgrade, which takes effect immediately per FR-9's "Upgrade unlocks immediately" rule.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Store webhook delayed | Last verified entitlement honored within a signed grace window; reconciliation job resolves any lingering ambiguity (FR-6) |
| Duplicate webhook delivery | Idempotent on `provider_event_id`, safe no-op on replay (Edge Case 9) |
| Payment failure on renewal | Email/push reminder, grace period (`PastDue`), no child-mode billing messaging at any point |
| Restore-purchase request | Server-side receipt re-validation, entitlement re-established without a new purchase |
| Plan-capacity-reducing downgrade with more active children than the new plan allows | Parent prompted to select which children remain active; deterministic 24-hour fallback if no selection |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero invoice history yet (new subscriber, first billing cycle not yet processed) → friendly "Your first invoice will appear here after your trial converts" framing.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Plan Comparison/Subscription screen: skeleton plan-card shimmer while entitlement/plan data loads.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Subscription screen renders last-cached entitlement/plan state when offline; purchase/upgrade/cancel actions require connectivity and clearly indicate this if attempted offline, given their store-billing-API dependency.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; all purchase actions route through the OS-level Play Store/App Store billing sheet, which has its own standard permission/account context outside this app's control.

functional_requirements.requirement: Plan Comparison (canonical, source §6.9 "Plan Comparison" table): Free Family Starter ($0, 1 active child, basic stories/duas/habits/basic reports, premium content locked, no AI weekly reports, limited offline); Mobile Family ($3/mo or $30/yr, 16.7% savings, 4 children, expanded content, 10 offline downloads, monthly family report, limited AI insights); Premium Family ($5.99/mo or $59/yr, 17.9% savings, 8 children, full story/Quran library, premium animated stories, full offline mode, weekly AI parent reports, advanced dashboard, extra child slots addable later).

Subscription Lifecycle state machine (canonical, source §6.9): `Free → Trial (7-day) → ActivePaid → RenewalPending → ActivePaid (auto-renew success) | PastDue (payment fails) → ActivePaid (recovered) | Free (grace ends); ActivePaid → Canceled → Free (paid period ends); ActivePaid → DowngradeScheduled → Free (next cycle)`.

**Trial Rules** (canonical, source §6.9/§"Yearly Subscription Logic"): (1) parent sees trial length, post-trial price, renewal date, and auto-renew disclosure before confirming; (2) parent confirms through the platform purchase flow (Google Play / App Store) — **never a custom payment form**; (3) trial entitlements (Mobile Family level) activate immediately; (4) on day 7, Mobile Family auto-activates if billing succeeds; **store receipt + signed webhook are the billing source of truth, not client-reported state**.

**Cancellation/Downgrade Rules** (canonical, source §6.9 table): Cancel subscription → paid access remains until the period ends, then reverts to Free limits; Trial cancellation with multiple children → parent selects 1 child to remain active on Free, others become **disabled, not deleted** (progress retained, restored when plan capacity returns), deterministic fallback (most-recently-active child) applies if no selection within 24 hours; Payment failure → parent receives email/push reminder, **child mode never shows billing messaging**; Renewal reminder → annual plans notify 7 days and 24 hours before renewal; Free plan second-child attempt → upgrade prompt shown in **parent mode only**, existing child's data unaffected.

**Entitlement checks apply at:** catalog/home feed, search, content detail, playback start, download manifest, AI features, and child-profile activation/creation (source §6.9 Validation Rules — the canonical, complete list of entitlement checkpoints every consuming feature must implement).

**Store webhook delayed → use last verified entitlement plus a grace window, then reconcile via a dedicated reconciliation job (not silent trust of the webhook alone, since webhook delivery is not guaranteed-once)** (source §6.9 Error Handling).

**The web portal cannot initiate app-store purchases outside provider policy; it may display the active entitlement and direct the parent to the mobile app appropriately. Store-purchase actions route through platform billing APIs only** (source §5 Web business rules / NoorHeroes Blueprint Parent Area screen table — restated as the hard rule governing the web portal's strictly limited billing surface).

**Purchases, AI controls, external links, deletion/export, and profile edits require parent PIN. Child mode never exposes billing or account-management controls** (source NoorHeroes Blueprint — restated as the hard rule this feature's child-mode-invisibility guarantee enforces, consistent with A.2's platform-wide no-billing-content-to-child rule).

**Yearly Billing Flow** (canonical, source §"Billing Flow" card): Trial converts automatically to Mobile Family unless the parent cancels before the trial ends; Auto-renew renews unless the parent cancels before the renewal date; Cancel means access continues until the paid period ends, then returns to Free limits; Upgrade unlocks immediately and keeps all child profiles intact; Trial cancellation/downgrade activates Basic Free with only one child remaining active and additional profiles disabled without data deletion.

**Downgrade never deletes child data; excess profiles become read-only archives, never silently deleted** (source NoorHeroes Blueprint Subscription & Billing screen, "Navigation Rules" — restated; cross-ref C.21's archived-profile read-only display pattern).

Subscription screen components (canonical, source screen catalog): plan card, entitlement list, invoice history, "Manage on Play Store" deep link, cancel flow. Actions: start trial, upgrade, downgrade, cancel renewal, view invoice, retry failed payment. Entry points: Parent Dashboard, paywall upsell, Settings. Exit points: Google Play billing sheet (external), Parent Dashboard.

Billing endpoints (canonical, source API table): `GET /api/v1/billing/plans` (public, cached); `POST /api/v1/billing/subscribe` (Bearer JWT, validates receipt server-side before activation); `POST /api/v1/billing/webhooks/play` (webhook signature, idempotent on `provider_event_id`, feeds reconciliation); `POST /api/v1/billing/reconcile` (internal/Celery, scheduled job reconciling entitlement state vs. provider truth, not user-facing).

Paywall upsell UI is shown **only in the parent area** when a profile limit is reached or premium content is browsed in a parent-approved discovery context — never inside child mode (cross-ref A.2's hard rule, C.20's explicit permission for parent-surface billing messaging).

Premium content items remain **visible with a lock icon** in parent-approved discovery contexts — never hidden entirely. **Locking never deletes progress. Free plan always supports basic Islamic education** (source NoorHeroes Blueprint — restated, cross-ref A.3/A.10's established "locked, not hidden" content pattern).
